To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We model the adverserial machine learning problem by allowing an adversary to manipulate the data distribution, (2) We show that the optimal operational decision is a linear function of the probabilistic classifier output, and (3) We experimentally demonstrate that our approach outperforms the previous state of the art in adversarial machine learning.
we develop and evaluate an algorithm that is simple, scalable, and robust against adversarial attacks.

we can use a linear optimization program to compute optimal operational decisions in adversarial environments, that our approach is simple, highly scalable, outperforms the previous state of the art, and that it has been implemented in a real-time operational environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a general framework for using machine learning in operational decision support systems that are subject to adversarial manipulation of data and/or the learning algorithm.
the use of machine learning in operational decision-making in adversarial environments.
developing machine learning algorithms that are robust to adversarial manipulation and can be used for operational decision-making in adversarial environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our work is an important contribution to the literature on adversarial learning and machine learning for operational decisions, and we hope that the ideas presented here will be of interest to a wide range of practitioners.
we present an algorithm for making operational decisions based on predictions of an arbitrary probabilist classifier that is more robust to adversarial manipulation than existing methods.
our work is a major step forward in addressing the adversarial learning problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed approach is able to achieve a higher level of robustness to adversarially crafted data, compared to the state of the-art, while maintaining a high level of performance on the data that is not adversarial.
we provide a framework for operational decision making in adversarial environments, and we provide the first experimental evaluation for this problem.
we propose a novel adversarial machine learning framework that is more realistic and practical than previous approaches, and we demonstrate that it is effective in adversarial settings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in adversarial environments, it is better to focus on the optimal use of imperfect information rather than improving the accuracy of a classifier.

, when the adversary is unconstrained, the best approach to adversarial machine learning is to use the output of a probabilistic classifier in a linear optimization model that computes optimal operational decisions.

the adversarial machine-learning literature should not be concerned with the robustness of learning algorithms, but rather with the robustness (and scalability) of the operational decisions that use the predictions from such algorithms.
